Tanya Lloyd

Democratic candidate for U.S. Representative, District 27, Travis County, Texas · Challenger

Public school teacher (Lockhart ISD)

Tanya Lloyd is a public school teacher from Lockhart, Texas, who describes herself as a fifth-generation Texan. She was the Democratic nominee for Texas' 27th Congressional District in 2024 and lost the general election to incumbent Michael Cloud. On March 3, 2026, she won the Democratic primary with about 63% of the vote, defeating Eustaquio Castro-Mendoza and Wayne Raasch, and faces Cloud again on November 3, 2026.

Where Lloyd stands

Education
Supports fully funding public schools and early education for all children. Supports keeping the U.S. Department of Education and opposes school voucher programs.
Healthcare
Says healthcare is a universal right, not a privilege. Lists expanding rural healthcare as a campaign priority.
Abortion / reproductive rights
Supports guaranteed access to abortion and full reproductive rights.
Economy and wages
Supports a living wage for every job and universal daycare for families.
Agriculture
Proposes farm policy that rewards conservation and lowers taxpayer costs. Wants large agribusinesses to pay farmers what she calls the real price for raw goods.
Democracy
Lists strengthening democracy as one of her campaign priorities.

Background

  • Occupation: elementary/public school teacher, Lockhart Independent School District
  • Earlier career: worked at car dealerships and in real estate
  • Education: Lockhart High School; bachelor's degree, Texas State University (2006)
  • 2024: Democratic nominee for U.S. House, Texas District 27; lost the general election to Michael Cloud
  • 2026: Won the Democratic primary for U.S. House, Texas District 27 (March 3, 2026; 63.1%)
  • Has not held elected office

Also running for U.S. Representative, District 27

  • Michael Cloud Republican
